mainEntity.name: What does an APAC crypto PR program actually cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: An APAC crypto PR program covers nine workstreams. One: native-language placement in tier-1 Korean crypto outlets (BloomingBit, TokenPost, BlockMedia, Coinness, CoinReaders). Two: Japan trade press placement (CryptoTimes JP, Coinpost, Iolite). Three: Greater-China bilingual diaspora coverage through ChainCatcher, Jinse, PANews and Foresight News. Four: India home-market PR across Inc42, YourStory, Economic Times, Business Today, Forbes India, Mint. Five: Southeast Asia coordination via e27, Tech in Asia, KrAsia and DealStreetAsia. Six: MENA placement and Token2049 Dubai leverage through Arabian Business, Gulf News and Cointelegraph Arabic. Seven: regional KOL waves with native-language briefs and per-market disclosure compliance. Eight: on-ground event placements at Korea Blockchain Week, Token2049 Singapore, Token2049 Dubai, Japan Blockchain Week, ETHIndia and Consensus Hong Kong. Nine: country-specific compliance navigation for the Q2 2026 regulatory overhaul in South Korea (FSC five-minute reconciliation), Japan (Payment Services Act to FIEA migration), Hong Kong and Australia.

mainEntity.name: Which APAC markets does the practice cover and why those specifically?

acceptedAnswer.text: Six core APAC markets plus MENA. South Korea generates roughly half of all tracked crypto-native media traffic across Asia, so it is the single biggest unlock for any Web3 founder serious about the region. Japan is the second-largest, with regulatory weight rising as the JFSA migrates crypto oversight to the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act in 2026. Vietnam is the highest-growth retail market in SEA with Telegram-led adoption patterns. China and the Greater-China diaspora reach is run through bilingual outlets like ChainCatcher and Jinse rather than mainland-licensed press. Singapore is the regional event hub (Token2049) and a credibility anchor under MAS. India is the home market for the practice and a category-builder market for any AI startup serious about a real engineer audience. MENA, anchored on Dubai and Abu Dhabi, is the fastest-moving Web3 regulatory perimeter and the right market for RWA and tokenization plays after the MANTRA Middle East story showed how a category framing can be won out of the region.

mainEntity.name: How much does APAC crypto PR cost in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three commercial models. APAC Quarterly Retainer runs $6,000 to $14,000 per month over a three to six month engagement and covers two to three named-market placements per quarter, plus always-on event-circuit coordination across Korea Blockchain Week, Token2049 Singapore, Token2049 Dubai, Japan Blockchain Week and Consensus Hong Kong. Single-Market Launch Sprint runs $12,000 to $35,000 total for one focused 14 to 21 day window — typical use case is a Korea-only or Japan-only push timed to a mainnet, a listing or a regional event. Always-On Market Coordinator runs $3,000 per month with a three-month minimum and books the senior-operator slot plus one curated market wave per quarter. Translation costs (native Korean, Japanese, Vietnamese, Mandarin and Arabic press copy) and regional KOL fees sit on top — published 2026 APAC KOL rates are nano $200-$1,500 per deliverable, micro $500-$5,000, mid $10,000-$30,000, macro $25,000-$100,000 plus, with a 15 to 25 percent premium in Korea and Japan over Western benchmarks.

mainEntity.name: How does APAC crypto PR handle the Q2 2026 regulatory deadlines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Q2 2026 is the most-overlapping regulatory window APAC crypto has seen. South Korea's Financial Services Commission ordered all exchanges to implement five-minute automated balance reconciliation, automatic kill-switches and monthly external audits by end of May 2026, alongside a zero-threshold Crypto Travel Rule. Japan's JFSA is migrating crypto oversight from the Payment Services Act to the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act, with crypto assets reclassified closer to securities. Hong Kong's SFC is tightening VASP licensing and stablecoin frameworks. Australia's Treasury is finalising the digital-asset platform regime. Every APAC announcement Shilika ships in 2026 carries a per-market compliance note: what is sayable in Korea, what is not sayable in Japan post-FIEA, what gets a license-language footnote in Hong Kong, what cannot be framed as a securities offering in Australia. The compliance review is not optional and is not delegated to the founder.

mainEntity.name: How is APAC PR different from running a single global press release?

acceptedAnswer.text: A single global press release translated into Korean and Japanese fails in APAC because each market has its own news values, regulatory line, journalist roster and event calendar. Korean trade press wants exchange-listing detail and a regulatory-status quote. Japanese trade press wants a partner-name credibility anchor and a clean-data table. Indian press wants founder-country detail, raise lead investor and SEBI-adjacent regulatory framing. MENA press wants a UAE or Saudi regulatory tie-in and a named local partner. The Outset PR 2026 APAC traffic report (published January 2026) found audience consolidation around the top 20 outlets, which means a region-mapped pitch list of 20 to 35 named outlets across six markets outperforms a generic 200-outlet blast by an order of magnitude. Native translation alone is not a PR strategy. A market-by-market framing is.

mainEntity.name: Does APAC PR earn AI-search citations in Korean, Japanese and Mandarin AI engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, increasingly so. Naver, Kakao and LINE in Korea and Japan respectively are building generative answer surfaces that lean heavily on native-language editorial. Baidu's Ernie and the bilingual surfaces of ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude all cite native-language sources when the query is asked in the local language. A campaign that produces named-byline placements in BloomingBit, TokenPost, CryptoTimes JP, Coinpost, ChainCatcher and Jinse seeds those answer engines with the citations they rank against. The Princeton GEO study (Aggarwal et al., arXiv:2311.09735) found pages combining citations, statistics and named quotations get cited 30 to 40 percent more by generative engines. The same dynamic holds for region-native AI engines, and the moat is even sharper because most Western PR programs never produce native-language editorial in the first place.

mainEntity.name: How does Korea crypto PR work in 2026 (FSC, DABA, exchange listings, KBW)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Korea PR in 2026 is anchored on three live regulatory beats and one event cycle. The Korea country desk at https://www.shilikajain.com/korea covers it in full: the Digital Asset Basic Act (DABA), the FSC's May 2026 zero-threshold Travel Rule and the five-minute automated balance reconciliation deadline, the second-phase legislation work on KRW-stablecoin issuance through licensed banks, and the Korea Blockchain Week 2026 press cycle in Seoul (September 22 to 28, anchored on Impact at COEX). The right outlets are BloomingBit, TokenPost, BlockMedia, Coinness and CoinReaders. The press calendar pivots on the Korean exchange listing answer (Upbit, Bithumb, Coinone, Korbit, Gopax), the Korean-language press kit, the founder Korean-press headshot and a Korean Telegram-and-Naver KOL wave timed to embargo lift at 10 AM KST. Naver and Kakao AI surfaces preferentially cite Korean-original editorial. APAC Quarterly Retainer runs $6,000 to $14,000 per month.

mainEntity.name: How does Japan crypto PR work in 2026 (FSA, FIEA, NISA spot ETF, WebX)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Japan PR in 2026 runs against the Cabinet-approved April 2026 FIEA reclassification of 105 crypto assets including BTC and ETH as financial instruments, the June 1 2026 Payment Services Act amendments that opened the foreign trust-type stablecoin route, the 20 percent flat capital-gains tax reform replacing the progressive 55 percent rate, and the spot BTC and ETH ETF NISA Growth-tier pipeline through SBI and Nomura that unlocks 12.5 million retail accounts. The Japan country desk at https://www.shilikajain.com/japan covers it in full. WebX 2026 (July 13 to 14, The Prince Park Tower Tokyo, 13,160 attendees from 88 countries) is the press cycle anchor. Outlets are CoinPost, CoinDesk Japan, Cointelegraph Japan, CryptoTimes JP, Iolite, Nikkei and Nikkei Cross Tech. Japanese press wants a partner-name credibility anchor and a clean-data table, not a hero-narrative pitch. note.com is the highest-leverage AI-search citation unlock per dollar; LINE Open Chat is the closed-community primary hub.

mainEntity.name: How does Singapore crypto PR work in 2026 (MAS, Project Guardian, Token2049)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Singapore PR in 2026 is anchored on MAS licensing status as the credibility frame, the Project Guardian tokenization workstreams as the institutional narrative bridge, and Token2049 Singapore (October) as the regional press cycle. The Singapore country desk at https://www.shilikajain.com/singapore covers it in full. Outlets are e27, Tech in Asia, DealStreetAsia, Token2049 newsroom and the regional crypto desks. Singapore press wants a MAS-licensing status quote, a regional-headquarters claim and an event-tied exclusive. A generic raise without a Singapore anchor reads as a press blip. The press copy lives or dies on three lines: MAS status (DPT licence, exemption status or Project Guardian participation), Singapore-as-regional-headquarters framing for tax and corporate-structure clarity, and the named local-partner anchor that ties the announcement to the Singapore ecosystem rather than treating Singapore as a generic Asia stop.

mainEntity.name: How does Dubai and MENA crypto PR work in 2026 (VARA, ADGM, RAK DAO, Token2049 Dubai)?

acceptedAnswer.text: MENA PR in 2026 is anchored on three regulators (VARA in Dubai, ADGM's FSRA in Abu Dhabi, RAK DAO in Ras Al Khaimah), the May 2026 Token2049 Dubai press cycle, and the regional category position the MANTRA $11M raise established (Abu Dhabi-based lead investor as a Middle East RWA story). The Dubai and MENA regional desk at https://www.shilikajain.com/dubai-mena covers it in full. Outlets are Arabian Business, Gulf News, The National and Cointelegraph Arabic, plus regional re-reports through CryptoPotato and Decrypt MENA. MENA press wants a UAE or Saudi regulatory tie-in, a named local partner and a Token2049 Dubai stage moment. Press copy carries a per-jurisdiction note: VARA for Dubai-licensed operations, FSRA for ADGM-domiciled vehicles, RAK DAO for DAO-structured tokenized treasuries. Single-Market Launch Sprint runs $12,000 to $35,000.

mainEntity.name: How does India crypto PR work in 2026 (SEBI, MeitY, Inc42, ETHIndia)?

acceptedAnswer.text: India PR in 2026 is anchored on three press tracks (mainstream business, startup-and-VC, crypto-native) plus the ETHIndia December press cycle. The India country desk at https://www.shilikajain.com/india covers it in full. The mainstream-business track is Economic Times, Business Today, Forbes India and Mint. The startup-and-VC track is Inc42, YourStory and Moneycontrol. The crypto-native track is CoinGape, NewsBTC India and HackerNoon for founder interviews. Indian press wants founder country of origin, lead-investor name and SEBI-and-MeitY-adjacent regulatory framing. The Bullieverse $4M seed was launched as an Economic Times exclusive then run on two parallel tracks (mainstream Indian business plus crypto-native) each with its own framing of the same fact sheet. Indian retail audiences route through X, YouTube and Telegram tri-platform creators, not a single channel.

mainEntity.name: How does Greater China crypto PR work in 2026 (ChainCatcher, Jinse, Hong Kong SFC)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Greater China PR in 2026 is run through bilingual diaspora-and-Hong-Kong-routed outlets, not mainland-licensed press. The right outlets are ChainCatcher, Jinse (jinse.cn), PANews and Foresight News. Hong Kong is the licensing anchor: the SFC tightened VASP licensing and the stablecoin framework moved into force in 2026, so any HK service-provision claim needs a license-language footnote or it gets re-reported with the gap noted. Mandarin-original copy outperforms translated Western press kits because Baidu's Ernie and the bilingual surfaces of ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude cite Mandarin-native editorial for Mandarin queries. Press copy carries no mainland-promotion language by design (that is a hard line not a stylistic preference). The Consensus Hong Kong cycle (February) is the highest-leverage regional press window of the first quarter, paired with a tier-1 Western re-report (CoinDesk, The Block) on the founder-on-stage moment.

mainEntity.name: Which APAC AI engines should an AI or Web3 founder be cited in by name?

acceptedAnswer.text: Six surfaces in priority order. Naver in Korea (the dominant Korean search-and-answer surface, with a heavy preference for Korean-original editorial). Kakao's evolving answer surface (closed-community-leaning, KakaoTalk integration). LINE in Japan (closed-community plus LINE AI summary cards). Baidu's Ernie in mainland China (Mandarin-original editorial preference, no English-original citation behaviour). The bilingual surfaces of ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Google AI Mode when the query is asked in the local language (they cite native-language sources, not English back-translations). Apple Intelligence and the Samsung-LINE Korean route for mobile-anchored regional queries. The 25-prompt AI citation buyer panel (Plan Week 9.1) runs against ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Gemini in English; the regional panel adds Korean, Japanese and Mandarin variants for native-surface coverage.
